paragraphs: A new report by the European Union Drugs Agency reveals that cocaine use is rising fast across Europe.
Based on drug residues found in city wastewater. Spanish and Belgian cities recorded the largest samples; the Spanish town of Lleida topped the continent’s chart.

Spain has become the main hotspot for the drug, as Barcelona and Lleida saw the steepest increases in consumption. Other growing areas were discovered in Denmark and Slovenia. While wastewater shows where the most drugs are used, a population survey showed that Norway and the Netherlands actually have the highest consumption rates among adults.

To fight this problem, police are tracking new trafficking routes. Drug gangs are increasingly using smaller ports, drones, and boats to land on remote beaches in Spain and Portugal to avoid detection. A massive police operation recently hit a major route across the ocean, known as the Atlantic Cocaine Highway. 54 people were arrested and 11 tonnes of cocaine seized.

paragraphs: A new European study shows that cocaine use is growing very fast. Scientists looked at wastewater in different cities to find out where people use this illegal drug the most.

Cities in Spain and Belgium have the highest numbers. The top city is Lleida in Spain, followed closely by Antwerp and Amsterdam. The data shows that Spain is the main hotspot, and cities like Barcelona show a big increase in drug use. A survey showed that Norway and the Netherlands had the most users, especially among young people.

This drug market causes a lot of gang violence and crime. Drug smugglers are now using smaller boats, drones, and new routes to bring drugs into Europe through small ports and quiet beaches. Recently, a big police operation stopped a famous sea route called the Atlantic Cocaine Highway and arrested 54 people.
